aldemar.headline: The US strikes Iranian minelayers and the war restarts — oil jumps, hike odds hit 62%
aldemar.standfirst: Sunday's strike on two IRGC launchers at Larak Island was the first US military action against Iran since late July, and it reset everything last week's de-escalation had priced. CENTCOM called it a "limited, precise action" against minelaying forces posing an "imminent threat"; the IRGC promised "the punishment of the aggressor" and fired ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan — eight intercepted, no damage. Brent went back above $88 and WTI added 2.87% to 85.93, pushing September hike odds to roughly 62%. The Dow fell 0.7% and the S&P 0.3%, though August still closed up 2.5%. In the book, GOOG dropped 2.18% on an FTC report — the largest single-name move you hold.

positions.title: Nothing that matters on BAC, PLTR, AAPL — 3 items, all filed as noise

items.html: BAC — BAC −0.61% to 61.94 with hike odds climbing to 62%. A quiet give-back inside Friday's range, low 61.90, holding the 62 area it reclaimed. The macro is still moving the right way for the thesis — the oil spike pushed September hike odds from 57% to about 62% and the 10-year added 3bp — but the stock is not yet being paid for it. Gabriel −3.79% on entry at −0.61R, stop 60.39 2.6% below; Aldemar −3.46% at −0.49R, stop 59.65 3.8% below. Friday's jobs report is the next thing that moves this: it decides the September meeting, and the September meeting is what this position is really long.

PLTR — PLTR +0.05% to 186.38 — a third quiet session at the top of the breakout. No news, no give-back: 183.79 low, 187.94 high, closing within a dollar of Friday. Consolidating a +4.75% breakout without surrendering it is what a healthy momentum position looks like. Provisional entry near 184 is +1.29%. It still has no stop recorded, which is the one thing to fix — a name that ran 10% in three sessions can retrace that in one.

AAPL — AAPL −0.89% to 316.85 as John Ternus takes over as CEO today. The handover from Tim Cook completes on 1 September and the market marked the stock down slightly into it, with a 312.80 low. Provisional entry near 321 is −1.29%. Nine days to the product event; nothing has changed about the setup except that the entry is now underwater and still has no defined risk.

themes.right: kinetic again · Larak Island strike · missiles at a US base in Jordan
themes.title: Zero tolerance meets a promise of punishment

items.html: US forces destroy two Iranian launchers on Larak Island preparing to deploy sea mines into the strait — the first strike on Iran since late July. CENTCOM framed it as a "limited, precise action" against IRGC minelaying forces posing an "imminent threat", carried out to protect "civilian mariners, commercial shipping, and the free flow of global commerce". It follows the US completing mine clearance of the strait's main shipping lane and Trump declaring a "Zero Tolerance policy on mine placement".

Iran fires ballistic missiles at a US base in Jordan; eight intercepted, no damage or casualties. The IRGC said the strike "will be answered by the sons of Iran and will result in the punishment of the aggressor", then answered proportionally and ineffectively. A response calibrated to be intercepted is a response designed not to end the diplomacy — but it is still the first exchange of fire in five weeks.

Brent back above $88, WTI +2.87% to 85.93 — the biggest single-day gain since the deadline lapsed. Crude reversed most of last week's 4% decline in one session. The move is rational: the corridor framework assumed a strait that gets safer, and Sunday demonstrated it is being made safe by force rather than by agreement.

themes.note: The transmission is oil → inflation → the regime call, and it just reconnected. Ten days ago crude at $93 was holding the inflation gate open; last week's de-escalation took it to $80 and the market started pricing relief; Sunday put it back to $86 and hike odds to 62%. Note the important nuance, though — the US is striking to keep the strait open, not to close it. If the mine clearance holds and the corridor still opens, this is a violent step toward the constructive outcome rather than away from it. Friday's jobs report now matters more than the next headline out of Muscat.

world.title: August closes green, September opens with a war and a live Fed

items.html: September hike odds climb to about 62%, up from roughly 40% a week ago; the 10-year adds 3bp to 4.76%. The oil spike did what Jackson Hole started. A hike is now the market's base case with fifteen days to the meeting, and the path runs through Friday's employment report — the last major data point before the decision.

Dow −0.7%, S&P −0.3%, Nasdaq −0.1% on the day; for August, Nasdaq +3%, S&P +2.5%, Dow +1.3%. A month that contained an AI financing panic, a war escalation, a consumer scare and a hawkish Fed still finished up 2.5%. Tech held up best on Monday despite the rate move, which says the Nvidia guidance is doing more work than the macro right now.

FTC reported to be finalising a potential lawsuit against YouTube over content-policy disclosures. The probe has run since last year and concerns whether users were misled about what they could post before removals and suspensions. No remedy has been signalled, and the FTC declined to discuss it. Regulatory risk on Alphabet has been dormant since the antitrust remedies passed — this reopens it.

Friday's employment report is the decisive data point for the September FOMC. With hike odds at 62% and CPI on the 11th, the labour print is the one number that can still move the meeting either way. It lands into a book that is long a bank, long two momentum names without stops, and long a megacap that just acquired a regulator.

weekly.headline: The war stopped setting the price and the Fed started — and the AI audit closed
weekly.standfirst: Three things resolved in five sessions. Washington launched its "economic D-Day" sanctions on Monday and crude fell, because the barrels were already blockaded. Iran and Oman then put an actual reopening mechanism on the table — a joint corridor plus mine clearance, permanent route inside 30 to 60 days — and oil finished the week down 4.05%. Nvidia answered the AI financing question with $96.2bn of revenue and a $108bn guide, ending the audit that had run all August. Then on Friday the Fed chair walked into Jackson Hole and doubled September hike odds to 57%. The book ends the week with one closed trade, both BAC positions recovered off Thursday's break, two new names added — PLTR on Thursday and AAPL on Friday, both still provisional — and a new question: rates, not war.
